title: Components of injective towers are acyclic
statement:
Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and schemes $T,S$, and put $R_{T,r}=\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^r$ and $R_{S,r}=\mathcal O_{E,S}/\ell^r$ as in [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], with the canonical identification $g^{-1}R_{S,r}\simeq R_{T,r}$ for every morphism $g:T\to S$. Use the small pro-etale sites with the size convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $I_\bullet$ be an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$. Then for every $r\geq1$, the component $I_r$ is a direct summand of a finite product of sheaves $J_n$ ($1\leq n\leq r$), each an injective $R_{T,n}$-module viewed as an $R_{T,r}$-module by restriction along $R_{T,r}\to R_{T,n}$. In particular $I_r$ is acyclic for sections over every object of $T_{\mathrm{proet}},$ hence $g_*$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic] for every morphism $g:T\to S$, where $g_*$ is the ordinary module direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] for the coefficient identification $g^{-1}R_{S,r}\simeq R_{T,r}$.

Here $g_{*,\bullet}$ denotes the additive left exact functor on coefficient towers obtained by applying these ordinary direct images levelwise, with the transitions induced by the original transitions; $Rg_{*,\bullet}$ denotes its total right derived functor on $D^+$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Evaluation and $C_n$ have the meaning of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Consequently, for $C_\bullet\in D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ with a bounded below injective resolution $C_\bullet\to I_\bullet^\cdot$, the complex $g_*I_n^\cdot$ represents $Rg_{*,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}C_n$, and there is a natural isomorphism
$$(Rg_{*,\bullet}C_\bullet)_n\simeq Rg_{*,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}C_n.$$

proof.text: Work in the common larger universe and small site models specified by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For either scheme and each coefficient ring sheaf, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] gives a Grothendieck abelian module category, hence enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. The tower categories are Grothendieck abelian by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], so the same enough-injectives theorem applies to them. Thus all module and tower injective resolutions used below exist in the stated categories.

source.place: Tag 079H, theorem-injective-embedding-grothendieck; blueprint proof, ambient coefficient categories

proof.text: Apply [det-sp-tower-evaluation-adjoint] to obtain a monomorphism $a:I_\bullet\hookrightarrow P_\bullet=\prod_{n\geq1}r_nJ_n$, with $J_n$ injective over $R_n$. By [def-sp-injective-resolutions], the identity of $I_\bullet$ extends across $a$, giving $b:P_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ with $ba=1$. Products of the systems in [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] are levelwise: the projections and a map into the product are defined componentwise, and compatibility with transitions is checked after each projection. Since $(r_nJ_n)_r=0$ for $n>r$ and equals the restriction of $J_n$ for $n\leq r$, evaluation of $ba=1$ exhibits $I_r$ as a retract of the finite product $\prod_{n\leq r}\operatorname{Res}_{R_r\to R_n}J_n$.

source.place: First paragraph: embedding, splitting, and finite product at each level

proof.text: For every object $U$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $q>0$, apply [lem-sc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic-zariski] to the ringed site $(T_{\mathrm{proet}},R_n)$ and the injective $J_n$. Despite its historical Zariski suffix, its statement is for an arbitrary ringed site and gives $H^q(U,(J_n)_{ab})=0$. Restriction along $R_r\to R_n$ leaves this abelian sheaf unchanged. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] with ring sheaf $R_r$ to deduce $R^q\Gamma_{R_r}(U,\operatorname{Res}J_n)=0$. The smallness, common-universe and enough-injectives hypotheses were established in step 1; no flatness of the quotient map or injectivity after restriction of scalars is asserted.

source.place: Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, second equality and proof of injective-module abelian acyclicity

proof.text: Fix $r,U$ and use injective $R_r$-module resolutions $L_n^\cdot$ of the finitely many restricted $J_n$. Their finite product is an injective resolution of $P_r$: maps into a finite product extend coordinatewise by [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and kernels and images in a finite sum of complexes are coordinatewise. Sections of this resolution and their cohomology are also finite products. The defining formula for derived functors in [def-sp-left-exact-additive] therefore gives $R^q\Gamma(U,P_r)=\prod_{n\leq r}R^q\Gamma(U,\operatorname{Res}J_n)=0$ for $q>0$. Applying the functor $R^q\Gamma(U,-)$ to the two maps splitting $I_r$ off $P_r$ factors its identity through zero, so $R^q\Gamma(U,I_r)=0$. This proves the section-acyclicity claim without any infinite-product exactness claim.

source.place: Second paragraph: finite products and direct summands preserve higher-section vanishing; explicit elementary argument

proof.text: Let $L^\cdot$ be an injective $R_r$-module resolution of $I_r$. By step 4 and the defining formula of [def-sp-left-exact-additive], $H^q(L^\cdot(U))=0$ for every $U$ and $q>0$. For an object $V$ of $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$, [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives $(g_*L^\cdot)(V)=L^\cdot(T\times_S V)$, whose positive cohomology therefore vanishes. Every positive-degree sectionwise cycle is a sectionwise boundary; since kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the positive cohomology sheaves of $g_*L^\cdot$ vanish. Thus $R^qg_*I_r=0$ for $q>0$, exactly $g_*$-acyclicity [def-sp-acyclic]. This is the sheafification-of-cohomology argument, written directly on the resolution.

source.place: Second paragraph, final sentence; compare Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images

proof.text: By exactness of evaluation in [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], $C_n\to I_n^\cdot$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $I_n^\cdot$ has the same lower bound as the tower resolution. Each term is $g_*$-acyclic by step 5. Apply [src-right-derived-functor-plus-acyclic-unit] to the additive left exact finite-level functor $g_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]: it identifies $g_*I_n^\cdot$ with $R^+g_*I_n^\cdot$, hence with $R^+g_*C_n$. The module categories are abelian with enough injectives by step 1. This bounded-below derived functor agrees with the ordinary derived direct image in the statement: a bounded-below complex of injectives is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so its image computes both constructions. The isomorphism uses the derived unit, and is natural.

source.place: Tag 015E, lemma-leray-acyclicity; Tag 05TH, lemma-injective-acyclic; blueprint proof, final paragraph

proof.text: The levelwise tower direct image defined in the statement is additive and left exact: both properties are checked at each level, using the section formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and the levelwise kernels of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Its source has enough injectives by step 1. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] therefore represents $Rg_{*,\bullet}C_\bullet$ by $g_{*,\bullet}I_\bullet^\cdot$. Exact evaluation gives its level-$n$ representative $g_*I_n^\cdot$. Step 6 identifies this complex with $Rg_{*,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}C_n$, proving the displayed isomorphism. The comparison is the one induced by the underived evaluation identity and the derived units. Their naturality, and the uniqueness clause (3) of the same right-derived-functor node, make it independent of the injective resolution and natural in $C_\bullet$.

source.place: Final paragraph: tower derived direct image, evaluation and the comparison; Stacks derived.tex Tags 05TI and 05TH
